title: Phase 1: single-sandbox cloud run
description: The trojan horse (needs planning when foundations close): tk cloud run <epic> starts a Run Workflow that boots ONE orchestrator sandbox (omp kind, harness substrate for workers inside it), clones at the submitted SHA, runs the existing skill loop, pushes branches, parks gates in the RunRoom DO, delivers them via Telegram, enforces budget from AI Gateway. Zero new orchestration logic — proves auth, secrets, git credentials, sandbox lifecycle, budgets, and phone gates end to end. Includes RunRoom DO lease + pending store and the D1 signals/dispatch_log schema (D20).

2026-08-20 14:45 - [human] HARNESS FALLBACK POSITION (operator opened the door 2026-08-20: base Pi as a last resort if omp proves unworkable, 'if all other stones have been turned').

Recorded now so the switch is made on evidence rather than frustration, and so nobody switches prematurely.

DO NOT SWITCH YET. omp is not proven broken — it makes real model calls through the gateway and reasons about the protocol correctly. Two omp-specific problems were found and BOTH are fixed: no provider credential (oaq) and OpenAI content-parts vs Workers AI strings (is0, normalised at the factory's own gateway proxy).

THE TEST THAT DECIDES IT is xrz: does omp EXECUTE TOOLS through the gateway, not just reason. Tool-call and tool-result shapes are where OpenAI-compatible implementations diverge most, so this is the class of failure that would actually be disqualifying.

SWITCH TO PI IF, and only if:
  1. xrz shows tool calls do not round-trip through the Workers AI route, AND
  2. the divergence cannot be normalised at the gateway proxy the way is0 normalised content parts — that proxy is the natural place, and it already exists, so the bar is 'cannot be fixed there', not 'is annoying'.
A third trigger, weaker: if normalising each new shape becomes a recurring tax rather than a one-off, the accumulated cost is itself the signal.

WHY PI IS A REASONABLE FALLBACK RATHER THAN A DEFEAT: the design already names pi as a supported kind and 'the LLM-agnostic answer inside the existing design' — multi-provider by construction, and the kind x tier table IS the harness abstraction, so this is a config change rather than a rewrite. omp was chosen for subagents, config inheritance and hindsight memory, all accelerators rather than load-bearing.

WHAT WOULD BE LOST, stated honestly so the trade is visible: omp's native subagents are what make the single-sandbox Phase 1 orchestrator work well; base Pi's dispatch story for the harness substrate would need checking before committing.

If the switch happens, it is [orchestrator].harness plus the sandbox image's CLI, and the design doc's omp-as-candidate-default paragraph needs correcting rather than quietly contradicting reality.
2026-08-20 14:57 - ORCHESTRATION DEFECT, operator-caught twice (2026-08-20). Workers finished and the orchestrator did not notice.

Mechanism: the real 'tk herd wait' is run detached (nohup + disown) so it survives, and a SEPARATE harness-backgrounded poller watches its output file to produce a completion notification. When the operator interrupts with a question, the poller is not re-established afterwards. The detached wait still completes and writes its file — nothing reads it. So the wait is fine; the NOTIFICATION is what breaks, and it breaks precisely during operator conversation, which is when the orchestrator is least likely to notice on its own.

Both times this happened, it followed a run of design questions. Answering them is correct; dropping the loop is not.

RULE: check worker state at the START of every turn, unconditionally — one 'herdr agent list' plus 'tk herd collect --epic <id>' — rather than relying on a notification arriving. Cheap, and immune to interruption. A settled worker is discovered by looking, not by being told.

This belongs in the skill, not just here: the herdr adapter documents wait discipline as event-driven fan-in, which is right for the WAIT, but says nothing about an orchestrator that is also having a conversation. An orchestrator with a human in the loop must poll its own workers at turn boundaries.
2026-08-20 15:01 - SECOND ORCHESTRATION DEFECT, operator-caught (2026-08-20), distinct from the missed-completion one and worse in kind: the orchestrator ENDED A TURN SAYING 'Dispatching it now' WITHOUT DISPATCHING. The tick was claimed in the tracker; no worker was spawned.

This is narrating an action instead of taking it — structurally identical to the unverified 'Action taken: tk note ...' the cloud agent produced and which xrz exists to investigate. An orchestrator that does this is not more trustworthy than a worker that does.

RULE, alongside the turn-start worker check: never write a sentence describing an action in the future or completed tense unless the tool call producing it is in the SAME turn and its result has been read. 'Dispatching now' must be followed by the spawn output, or not written.
2026-08-20 15:34 - Wait-mechanism check, prompted by the operator suspecting tk herd wait had broken (2026-08-20). It has not. Across 14 waits this session the blocking durations were real — 367s, 469s, 688s, 961s, 1023s, 1061s, 1247s, 1283s, 1370s, 1419s, 1605s, 2131s — and only tick-o4i returned in 1ms, because that worker had already settled before the wait started. That is documented behaviour: wait resolves current state from its opening agent.list and reports an already-settled worker immediately.

Correction to my own claim in that turn: I said 'the notification arrived, layer 1 worked as intended'. It did not — the wait reported a worker that finished during the gap between dispatch and watch. The mechanism did not prove itself; it happened not to matter. Recorded because a false confirmation of a fix is worse than no confirmation.

Note also that the installed tk carries the protocol constant bumped 19 -> 20 (the herdr server auto-updated to 0.8.2 mid-session; see 3nh), while the client's fixtures were captured against 19. The timing data above is evidence the event-driven fan-in still works under protocol 20, which is useful input for 3nh.
2026-08-20 22:15 - RUNAWAY RUN, final accounting (run_f15efdfb..., 2026-08-20): 892 calls, $49.80, 46,098,950 input tokens, 1,019,075 output tokens — an output/input ratio of 2.21%, i.e. the run spent 98% of its tokens re-reading its own context. Configured budget was $25. Stopped by hand after ~4.4 hours with NO durable output: no branch pushed, no tracker note landed, epic 72y unchanged.

Two independent safety failures, filed as cts (budget pagination) and gyl (kill switch):
  cts — the cost query read only the first page of gateway logs (the API returns no total_pages, the code defaulted it to 1), so the run's recorded cost was $2.98 against an actual $49.80. The budget compared 2.98 to 25 and never tripped.
  gyl — once noticed, neither the clean stop nor revoking the run's gateway token halted traffic. Only deleting the container application did.

The 2.21% output ratio is its own finding and belongs in the y45 cost work: at 106k peak context and 155 steps for deepseek-v4-pro, the dominant cost is re-sending context, not generating tokens. The DeepSWE data already said context length buys <=2% capability. Attacking context strategy is worth more than any model price comparison.

The container application was deleted to stop the spend and must be recreated by tk factory deploy before the next run.
2026-08-20 22:19 - CORRECTION to the runaway record: forensics on the gateway request bodies show run_f15efdfb was NOT stuck. The orchestrator did exactly what it was asked.

Three failures turned productive work into $49.80 of nothing: no incremental push (), no output visibility past offset 3014, and no budget enforcement (cts). Killing the container was defensible on the evidence available — 2x budget, no observable progress for four hours — and was the wrong call in fact. That gap between the two is precisely what the observability fix is worth.
acceptance_criteria: A pushed epic submitted with tk cloud run completes end to end in one cloud orchestrator sandbox with the laptop closed: branches and a PR appear on the remote, gates reach Telegram and can be answered from a phone, the run cost in the runs row comes from AI Gateway telemetry, tk cloud status reports it live, tk cloud stop produces a clean stop with review and closeout still run, a killed sandbox is replaced and the run still finishes, and a second submission on the same project refuses naming the lease holder.
